brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#0 (keyhole hanger, hex-acc-keyhole) on base piece:0,0,0;full hangs the cell on screws already in a wall. check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors.
The catalog has no clock movement, motor, dial, hands or spindle part, and no clock or watch prop (searched for 'clock', 'dial', 'motor', 'watch'). Nothing in the build turns.

There is no timekeeping part of any kind. The cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) is a plain closed face, not a clock face. It sits on the top of the cell, and the keyhole is on a side face, so it would not even face out from the wall.

finish.summary: Hex Cluster can't make a working clock. The catalog has no clock movement, hands or dial, and no clock prop. What I built is a single hex cell with a keyhole hanger, so it hangs on wall screws, and a plain top cover. It passed check_build with no mesh clashes. It's only a wall-hung box: it has no turning hands and can't tell the time. A real clock would need a clock movement from somewhere else, and nothing in this system is designed to hold one.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
